key_insight: Energy harvesting is moving from single-device materials innovation toward integrated, battery-independent microsystems that combine multiple ambient sources with smarter power management.
engineering_relevance: For IoT, wearables, and cyber-physical systems, the main challenge is no longer just harvesting more energy, but reliably delivering usable power through efficient PMICs, impedance matching, and durable storage.
method: Reviewed major harvester classes: TENGs, piezoelectric/pyroelectric devices, indoor photovoltaics, and RF rectennas.
Compared hybrid multi-source integration strategies for broader operating conditions.
Highlighted system-level advances in cold-start PMICs, metamaterial RF harvesting, and machine-learning-guided materials discovery.
evidence_signal: The abstract cites specific reported gains such as over 300% broader bandwidth for nonlinear piezoelectric oscillators and improved liquid-solid TENG designs that reduce wear.
watch_item: Hybrid harvesters can underperform in practice if cold-start circuitry, source matching, and storage degradation are not addressed under realistic field conditions.
paper_title: Energy Harvesting for Self-Powered Microsystems: A Critical Review of Materials, Power Management, and System Integration
